This guide covers running the program: the plugin's own screens in wp-admin, what every setting does, who can read what, and what to check when something looks wrong.

It also contains the mentor and student guides in full. Administrators are the people other people ask. Unless you are on the program as a mentor or a student too, no Student Report Card or Mentor Report Card is your own: you open anyone's through the Viewing as switcher, as Viewing a page as its owner describes.

Signing in

Nobody registers on this site, and there is no sign-up form: the program makes every account for the person it belongs to. That means two things on your first visit:

  1. Go to the site's login page and use Lost your password? with the email address on your account. A reset link arrives at that address.
  2. Set a password, and you are in - unless your account also asks for a code, which the next part covers.

If the reset email never arrives, the address on your account is probably not the one you are checking. The login page cannot change it - ask whoever runs the program.

Signing in with a code

Besides your password, your account may ask for a code. Whether it does is the program's choice, and it is made for every account of your kind at once. When it does, there is nothing to set up first: from your next sign-in, the code arrives by email. When it does not, signing in works as described above, and a card on your page invites you to turn the code on for yourself.

After you enter your username and password, a second screen asks for the code. Which kind depends on how your account is set up.

An emailed code. The screen says a verification code has been sent to the email address on your account. The email comes from this site and has Login confirmation code in its subject line. It holds a code of eight digits. Type it into Verification Code and press Verify. A code works once, and for fifteen minutes. Resend Code sends a new one and the new one replaces the old, so use the newest email.

An authenticator app. If you have set one up, the screen asks for the code from your app instead: Authentication Code. Open the app, find this site in it, and type the six digits it shows. The digits change every 30 seconds, so type the ones on the screen at that moment.

A wrong code does not lock you out for good, but the site makes you wait a moment before the next try, and the wait grows with every wrong code, up to fifteen minutes. Wait it out, then type the code again, carefully.

Setting up an authenticator app

An app on your phone is quicker than waiting for an email, and it keeps working when your inbox does not. The card at the top of your page starts it. Its heading is Add a second step to your sign-in when the code is yours to choose, and Your account asks for a code when you sign in when the program asks for one; its button, Turn on two-factor authentication or Set up an authenticator app, opens your profile screen at its Two-Factor Options. Ignoring the card costs nothing: signing in keeps working the way it does now.

If you already use emailed codes and you open that screen more than about ten minutes after you signed in, it first asks you to confirm with Revalidate now, which takes one more code. Then follow the steps on the screen: install an authenticator app on your phone (any will do, such as Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator), scan the QR code the screen shows with it, and type in the code your app then displays. Once the app is set up the card stops appearing.

Before you leave that screen, generate the recovery codes (the card calls them backup codes) and keep them somewhere other than your phone. Each works once, and the screen shows them only once. They are how you get back in if you lose the phone.

If you cannot get your code

  • The email does not come. Look in your spam folder, then press Resend Code. The email goes to the address on your account, so if you no longer read that mailbox, an emailed code cannot reach you.
  • Your phone or your app is gone. Under Having Problems? on the same screen, the site lists any other way your account has, for example Send a code to your email, or Use a recovery code if you saved some. Type one of your saved recovery codes where the screen asks for it, and cross that code off, because it will not work twice.
  • You have neither. Without the emailed code, the app or a recovery code, the site cannot tell that it is you, and it lets nobody past that screen. Tell whoever runs the program that you are locked out, and give them the username you sign in with. This guide cannot fix it for you.

Once you are signed in

Your page is drawn for whoever is signed in, so the same address shows each person their own page, and no change to a link shows anybody else's. The program's Administrators are the one exception: to help, they can open anyone's page, through a switcher only they are shown. A company's people share one Sponsor Dashboard: everyone the program attached to the company sees the same page.

The plugin in wp-admin

Everything the Administrator touches lives under one top-level menu, WPCredits Program. You need the wpcpm_manage_program capability to see it, which the Administrator role is granted on activation. Every screen under it is titled with its own name: Overview, a screen for each audience, Tools and a screen for each tool, and Settings.

On the forms named here, a press locks the button at once and the button says what it is doing until the next page opens, so a double press acts once: the decisions and the question on an opened application, on the Sponsors and Institutions screens; on the Mentors screen, the decisions on an application; on the Sponsors screen, Run again in the Moving sponsors onto the site box, Add the sponsor, a sponsor's Edit form and its Not a renewal, a sponsor's Attach account, Remove and posting switch, the offer and code forms, Draft a report and the forms of a report's editor, and the agreement forms; on the Institutions screen, the signed agreement's upload and withdrawal and the semester report buttons; Save, Send me a test and Restore the original in WPCredits Program > Tools > Emails; and the Track Builder's Create the track and Make the copy. Every other form works as it always has, searching, filtering, a list's Apply and Screen Options among them.

The words the screens use

The screens, the settings and this guide call each thing by one name.

Overview

WPCredits Program opens on the Overview: four cards with what waits for a decision, when each sync last ran and runs next, whether each tool can run, and the way to Settings. The Overview only reads and links; it decides nothing.

If Airtable is not connected yet, this screen says so and links straight to the setting.

Waiting for a decision lists each queue with something in it, in the order of the Administrator Dashboard's strip of counts, each as the strip reads its tile: the count first, set apart, then the strip's name for the queue, such as "2 Collaboration Agreements to review, 1 overdue". The count is the strip's own, so past 200 the sponsor posts and Sponsor Collaboration Agreements to review read 200+. Each is a link to where its queue is listed: the institution applications, agreements and mentor requests open the Waiting for review tab of the Institutions screen, the semester reports to review and the semesters due for drafting its Semester reports tab, and the locked accounts its Accounts tab; the mentor applications open the Waiting for review tab of the Mentors screen; the sponsor applications, posts, events and agreements open the Waiting for review tab of the Sponsors screen, each at the card that lists it, the sponsor reports to finish its Reports tab, and the offers running low its Offers and codes tab; the duplicated students open the Student Duplicate Finder; and the syncs that need a look open this screen's own Syncs card. The dashboard's strip draws a tile only for a count above zero, and this card likewise leaves out a queue with nothing in it; when nothing is waiting it says "Nothing is waiting for an Administrator right now." At the foot of the card, Decide on the Administrator Dashboard opens that page, where the decisions are made, except those on the mentor applications, which are made on the Mentors screen; while the page is missing, the card says so in the button's place and asks you to re-activate the plugin to recreate it.

Syncs has a row for each audience's sync, Students, Mentors and Institutions, each name a link to the screen the sync is run from: the Sync tab of the Students and Mentors screens and the Sync and storage tab of the Institutions screen. Last run gives the date and time of the last run, in the site's own formats, or Never. Next run gives the date and time of the next run; it says Not scheduled when none is, and Running now while a run is under way. The audiences' rows show no errors: a sync's last error is on the Administrator Dashboard's Syncs and health card. The fourth row, Outcome figures (1.122.24), is the weekly read of the three figures the site counts for its homepage with the WordPress Credits impact dashboard's definitions, every Monday at 07:00 UTC after the dashboard's build: its name opens the Connection tab of Settings, Last run is when the stored figures were read, a line under it says why the last attempt was held or failed, that it waits for the dashboard's build, that the site is not connected, which figure the homepage leaves out for having fewer than 30 answers or outcomes, or that the homepage shows none because the figures stored are more than 29 days old, and wp wpcredits outcome_figures shows them, reads them again with --refresh and checks them with --refresh --dry-run. The weekly read never stores the first figures: it holds them, and the line says to compare the counts with the dashboard's with wp wpcredits outcome_figures --refresh --dry-run and then store them with wp wpcredits outcome_figures --refresh. On the Administrator Dashboard's Syncs and health card the same line stands under the column headed Last error, and it is not always an error there: Waiting for the dashboard's Monday build., Not connected. and the note about fewer than 30 answers are notes, not errors.

Tools has a row for each tool, its name a link to the tool's screen, and under Status the line the tool's card shows on the Tools screen; for a tool that cannot run, that line is the warning that says why, in the tool's own words.

Settings says "Airtable is connected." or "Airtable is not connected yet." Its Open Settings button opens the Settings screen.

The audience screens

Since 1.92.0 the Administrator Dashboard on the front end gathers the queues these screens hold, apart from the mentor applications, which it counts (since 1.122.31) and which are decided on the Mentors screen; the Administrators screen links to it.

Since 1.93.0 the Sponsors screen is no longer a placeholder: it holds every sponsor with its status, program contact and accounts, the Create account and Attach account controls, on its Accounts tab since 1.122.0, and the log of interests sponsors expressed on their Sponsor Dashboard. Since 1.111.0 the sponsors' records live on this site, added with Add a sponsor and changed with Edit, both now on the Sponsors tab. An approved application creates its sponsor's account; any other sponsor's account is created on the Accounts tab's No account view, and nowhere else.

Since 1.97.0 the Sponsors screen also holds the queue of companies that applied through the form on the site, and its menu entry carries a bubble counting the applications, the signed agreements and the sponsor posts waiting for an Administrator, and since 1.123.0, while Sponsor tiers is on, the events waiting too, and since 1.123.18 the sponsor offers and the changes to them waiting for review. Since 1.122.0 that queue is read on the screen's Waiting for review tab and decided on the Administrator Dashboard, as the institution queue is.

Since 1.118.0 the Students screen is two tabs, and a press on either tab comes back to it. Accounts, the tab WPCredits Program > Students opens on, holds the Invitations card and the Student accounts list. Sync holds the last sync's error when it ended in one, the Airtable sync card with Sync students now, or the run's progress and Cancel sync while one is going, and the Last sync report.

The Student accounts list works like WordPress's own Users screen: every Student account, a page at a time, so each one can be reached however many the site has. Search students finds an account by name, username, email address or institution. The All, Invited and Never invited views split the list by whether an account has been sent an invitation, each with its count. The list opens sorted by name, A to Z, so a first press on the Student heading turns it Z to A; a press on Username or Institution sorts the list by it, A to Z, and pressing a heading again reverses the order. Screen Options sets how many rows a page holds, 20 by default, and which columns are shown; the Student column cannot be hidden, because each row's actions sit under it. The institution picker above the table, each institution with its number of accounts, narrows the list to one institution, and the Invitations card follows it, so its button invites only the students at that institution who have never been invited, and comes back to that institution's list. A student who also mentors and whose invitation was held when an application made them a mentor is left out of the button, and the card says how many it left out: only that student's own row sends it (see Becoming a mentor). The picker, a search by institution and the Institution sort work on the whole list, never only on the page in view.

Under each name are Edit, which opens the account in wp-admin, View page, which opens that student's Student Report Card, and Send invite or Resend invite, which emails that one student at once. To invite several, tick them, choose Send invite or Resend invite under Bulk actions and press Apply. On WordPress 6.7 or later, on this list and on every other accounts list, the action chosen under Bulk actions runs only when Apply is pressed: a search sent with rows ticked and an action chosen comes back to the list with nothing done to them, and Enter pressed in the menu does not apply it. Below 6.7, WordPress's own behavior stands. Send invite queues a first invitation for each ticked account that has never had one, as the card's button does, and the card shows the progress. Resend invite queues a fresh invitation for each ticked account invited before, which goes out with the next batch: the card's progress bar and its stop button follow a run of first invitations, and a re-invitation starts no run, so on its own it shows on neither. A row's invitation and the bulk actions both come back to the list as it was: the same view, search, institution, sort and page. However it is asked for, nobody is sent a second invitation within fifteen minutes of the last one: Resend invite on ticked accounts leaves out anybody invited in the last fifteen minutes, and its notice says how many it left out. Send invite and Resend invite on ticked accounts both leave out an account whose invitation was held when an application made it a mentor, and the notice says how many they left out: only that account's own row sends it, once an Administrator has confirmed the account is the person's.

In 1.119.0 the Mentors screen became two tabs in the same way, and a press on either tab comes back to it. Accounts, the tab WPCredits Program > Mentors opens on while no application to mentor waits (see Applications to mentor), holds the Invitations card and the Mentor accounts list. Sync holds, since 1.122.33, a warning while mentors made from applications have no Airtable row yet, with the way to where each is written, the last sync's error when it ended in one, the warning while institution and team names have not been read yet, the Airtable sync card with Sync mentors now, or the run's progress and Cancel sync while one is going, and the Last sync report.

Since 1.122.26 the Mentors screen has a third tab between them, Engagement. It opens with the figures the Administrator Dashboard's Mentor engagement card shows, then lists every mentor: Status, whether Airtable holds them as Active (and Administrator for an Administrator who also mentors), their Students now and before, their Last visit (the latest day they opened a page of the site while signed in, which the site notes once a day) and Last sign-in, their Schedule (weekly hours and a meeting link, or what is missing), the Notes they wrote, their one-to-one Calls held and to come with how many held calls have a note, and their Group sessions held and to come. The 7 days and the 30 days count whichever is later, a mentor's last sign-in or last visit, so a mentor on a remembered session is not shown as absent; a mentor for whom the site holds neither is counted as never signed in. Sort by Mentor, Students, Last visit, Last sign-in, Notes or Calls; the list opens with the most students first. Search mentors finds a mentor by name, username or email address. Screen Options sets how many rows a page holds, 20 by default, and which columns are shown; the Mentor column cannot be hidden. The views, each with its count, find who to follow up with: All, Active, With students now, Never signed in, Not seen in 30 days, No program action (no note, no saved schedule, no group session created and no call they canceled, including those who never signed in, so it can list more mentors than the card's count of those who signed in without one), Students, no weekly hours and Administrators. Every view but All and Administrators lists active mentors only, those Airtable holds as Active, and so do the figures above, except the call and group session figures, which count every call and group session on the site; an Administrator who also mentors is counted apart, and Administrators lists the active ones. All lists every mentor, active or not. The tab reads only. Sign-ins from before the release were read once from what the site already held and are approximate, and visits start with the release, so a date can read Not recorded yet; the note under the list gives the date of the reading. The site records the last sign-in and last visit of every account, not only mentors', and uninstalling the plugin removes them. wp wpcredits mentor_engagement --summary prints the same figures on the command line, and without --summary it prints one row per mentor, as a table, JSON or CSV; it writes nothing.

The Mentor accounts list works as the Student accounts list does: every Mentor account, a page at a time. Search mentors finds an account by name, username or email address. The All, Invited and Never invited views split the list by whether an account has been sent an invitation, each with its count. No students, the fourth view, with its count too, lists the mentors whose Students column shows 0: no current student, whether every student they had has finished or they never had one. The search, the sorts and the pages work in it as in the other views, and when every mentor has a current student it says so. The list opens sorted by name, A to Z, so a first press on the Mentor heading turns it Z to A, and Username sorts it by username, A to Z. Students sorts it by how many current students a mentor has, the fewest first, and Status puts Active before Not in Airtable; pressing a heading again reverses the order. Every sort works on the whole list, never only on the page in view. Screen Options sets how many rows a page holds, 20 by default, and which columns are shown; the Mentor column cannot be hidden, because each row's actions sit under it. The list has no institution picker, so the Invitations card counts, and its button invites, every mentor who has never been invited, except one whose invitation was held when an application made them a mentor: the card says how many it left out, and only that mentor's own row sends it (see Becoming a mentor).

Under each name are Edit, which opens the account in wp-admin, View page, which opens that mentor's Mentor Report Card, and Send invite or Resend invite, which emails that one mentor at once. To invite several, tick them, choose Send invite or Resend invite under Bulk actions and press Apply; both work as they do on the Students screen, through the same queue. A row's invitation and the bulk actions both come back to the list as it was: the same view, search, sort and page. Here too nobody is sent a second invitation within fifteen minutes of the last one, and Resend invite on ticked accounts says how many it left out; both bulk actions leave out a mentor whose invitation was held, and say how many.

Since 1.119.0 the Administrators screen is two tabs too, Accounts and Capabilities, under the Open the Administrator Dashboard button, which stays above them whichever tab is shown. The button is there while that page exists; while it is missing, the Administrator accounts list says so. Accounts, the tab WPCredits Program > Administrators opens on, holds the Administrator accounts list: every account with WordPress's Administrator role, a page at a time. Search administrators finds an account by name, username or email address. The list opens sorted by name, A to Z, so a first press on the Name heading turns it Z to A; a press on Username sorts it by username, A to Z, and pressing a heading again reverses the order. Screen Options sets how many rows a page holds, 20 by default, and which columns are shown; the Name column cannot be hidden, because each row's Edit, which opens the account in wp-admin, sits under it. Can manage program says whether each account holds the program's capability.

The list has one view, All, and no checkboxes, bulk actions or invitations: Administrators use WordPress's own Administrator role, the plugin never invites them, and their accounts are added and managed on the Users screen. Capabilities lists the program capabilities the Administrator role is granted on activation, as the screen did before.

Applications to mentor

Since 1.122.31 a person can apply to mentor on this site, at /become-a-mentor/, and an Administrator decides on each application on the Waiting for review tab of the Mentors screen. The form is off until Take mentor applications through the form on this site is switched on, under Mentor applications on the Students and mentors tab of Settings. While it is off, or while the syncs have read no countries or no contribution teams yet, the page shows the public nothing, and an Administrator who opens it one sentence saying why. The page is not gated: the people it is for have no account. The form writes nothing to Airtable. Since 1.122.33 a selected applicant who completes the mentors' course becomes a mentor on this site once Make mentors from applications is switched on, under Mentor applications on the Students and mentors tab of Settings, as Becoming a mentor, further down, describes. It is off until the launch, and while it is off an application stops at the mentors' course, as it did before 1.122.33, and nothing is written to Airtable.

The page the plugin makes starts with the Airtable form's introduction, two paragraphs above the form, and they are the page's to edit. So is the sentence an applicant reads once the form is sent: Thank-you sentence, in the Thank you panel of the Mentor Application Form block (or thanks="..." on the [wpcpm_mentor_application] shortcode), and while it is empty the plugin's own sentence is shown. A page already at /become-a-mentor/ when the plugin first looks is used as it is, so the form shows on it only once the block is added.

The form asks the eleven questions the Airtable form asks, in its order: the applicant's full name; their email; their WordPress.org profile (the username, an @username or the address of their profile on wordpress.org, kept as the username, and anything else refused with a sentence asking for one of those); their country (one field: type a few letters and pick one); whether they are a teacher at an institution taking part in the program; the languages they can mentor in; the contribution areas they have expertise in, which may be left empty; the hours a week they can give, from 1 to 40, kept to one decimal place; the compliance declaration, the GPL and trademark statement with its two links, which must be ticked; anything else they would like us to know; and the confirmation that they have read the WordPress.org privacy policy, which the line under the box links. An answer to Anything else you'd like us to know? holding what WordPress's cleaning would remove, a tag or a percent code, is refused: the form says so in a sentence that tells the applicant how to keep every word, and hands the typing back in its box. The countries are the ones the institution form offers and the contribution areas the teams a student picks from, both read by the syncs; the languages are a fixed list in the plugin, since the site holds none. It is guarded as the sponsor form is: a hidden field, a signed token, five submissions an hour per address and forty a day for the whole site before the rest are held, consent as a precondition with what was agreed to recorded, the comment disallowed list and the links counted, and a ceiling on acknowledgements. An application giving the address or the WordPress.org username of another application in the queue or waiting for the course, or of a mentor the site knows, is held with a mark and never merged. The thank-you page shows the application's reference (MAPP-2026-0007), and every application but one filed as spam is acknowledged by email with a link that confirms the address, unless the day's ceiling on acknowledgements has been reached or the email could not be handed to the mail queue; the addresses under Who is mailed, or every Administrator, are told of each one the checks did not hold, with the applicant's name and profile and the way to the tab.

WPCredits Program > Mentors opens on Waiting for review while any application waits there, and on Accounts while none does; the tab is first in the bar either way. It lists the applications oldest first, fifty at a time, in six views, each with its count: Waiting, every application not decided yet; Asked for more information and Second opinion, those two kinds among them; Selected (course pending), the applicants sent to the mentors' course; Activated, the applicants made mentors, which orders its list differently (see Becoming a mentor); and Lapsed. Under the list, in every view, Recently decided lists the fifty applications most recently declined or filed as spam, newest first, until they are deleted. Each application shows the name and reference, how long it has waited (for a selected one, the day it was selected and the day it lapses; for an activated one, the day it was made a mentor; for a decided one, the day it was declined or filed as spam), its marks (held, possible duplicate, already a mentor, address not confirmed and acknowledgement not sent), every answer, its history (each decision with its day, who took it and their note) and the decisions its state allows. The Administrator Dashboard's strip counts the applications waiting, and its tile opens this tab.

A selected application also shows what the Mentor Status Checker last found on the applicant's WordPress.org profile: Not checked yet, or the day of the last check and whether the course shows, does not show yet, or the profile could not be read, and why. While Make mentors from applications is off it says the applicant waits; and when the account for an applicant whose course showed could not be made, it says on which day and why, and the application stays selected.

The decisions, each with a box for a note where it takes one; a note stays on this site and is never sent:

  • Select sends the selection email, with the link set under Mentors' course invitation link, and moves the application to Selected (course pending). It is refused while that setting is empty, and it is offered on a lapsed application too, for an applicant who comes back, and on a declined one, for an applicant who appeals: an appeal is either a new application, if you ask them to apply again, or a note and Select on the same row.
  • Ask for more information sends the request for more information; the application stays in the queue, under Asked for more information, with the day it was asked.
  • Second opinion marks the application for a colleague and sends nothing. Its note, which says what to look at, is needed.
  • Decline sends the decline email and moves the application to Recently decided.
  • Mark as spam moves the application to Recently decided and sends nothing.
  • Put back in the queue, on an application filed as spam, returns it to Waiting, with a line in its history. One that was never acknowledged, and so carries the mark acknowledgement not sent, is sent the acknowledgement then, once, with the link that confirms the address; one acknowledged when it came, marked as spam by mistake, is sent nothing.
  • Send the acknowledgement, on an application still in the queue that carries the mark acknowledgement not sent, sends it now, once, with the link that confirms the address, and leaves the application where it is. It is for an application past the day's ceiling on acknowledgements, or whose hand-off to the mail queue was refused; one filed as spam is sent it by Put back in the queue. An application acknowledged already, or holding no address, is sent nothing, and two presses at one moment send it once.
  • The course is completed, on a selected application, and offered only while Make mentors from applications is on: for an applicant an Administrator knows has completed the mentors' course, whatever the profile shows. Its note, how you know, is optional and never sent. It makes the applicant a mentor at once, by the Administrator who pressed it, as Becoming a mentor describes.
  • Withdraw, on a selected application alone, moves it to Lapsed now and sends nothing. Its note, what the applicant wrote, is needed, and the public figures count it as lapsed. An application that another request is making a mentor at that moment is left as it is, and the press says so.
  • Write the Airtable row again, on an activated application whose Mentors row Airtable refused or never finished, writes it as the activation did; it takes no note, and a second press makes no second row (see Becoming a mentor).

Select, Ask for more information and Decline wait until the applicant has confirmed the address with the link in the acknowledgement: until then each is refused and says so. An application whose address is never confirmed is closed with Mark as spam, and a spam application counts for nothing in the public figures, so that applicant is not counted as having applied. An application marked acknowledgement not sent, one the form's checks filed as spam, one past the day's ceiling on acknowledgements, or one whose acknowledgement could not be handed to the mail queue when it was submitted, was never sent the link, so its address cannot be confirmed and the three decisions that email the applicant stay refused until it is: Put back in the queue sends it to an application filed as spam, and Send the acknowledgement to one still in the queue, past the ceiling or after a refused hand-off, and the mark goes either way. Select, Decline, Mark as spam, Withdraw, The course is completed and Send the acknowledgement ask before they act. The five emails are the Mentor applications area of Tools > Emails, where their words can be edited.

A selected application whose course has not shown after the days under Selected applications lapse after (days), 90 by default, moves to Lapsed by itself, with a line in its history, in the daily run that also keeps the days under Applications on the Advanced tab: spam is deleted after 30 days, and declined, lapsed and held applications after a year, by default. A selected application that is being made a mentor at that moment is left to that and does not lapse. The figures for the Credits Monthly Report and the WPCredits Tracker are public at /wp-json/wpcpm/v1/mentor-applications: for each month since the first application, how many applications were received, selected, activated (made a mentor), declined and lapsed, and how many applications are open and how many selected today, with nothing about any person. An application filed as spam is not counted as received. Each application counts once per figure in a month: one selected twice in a month counts once there, a withdrawal and a lapse in one month are one lapse, and one selected again in a later month, after a lapse or an appeal, counts in both months, so the months are not to be added up as if each application counted once. An applicant filed as already a mentor is not counted as made a mentor, and what happens to the Airtable row counts for nothing.

Becoming a mentor

With Make mentors from applications on, a selected applicant becomes a mentor in one of two ways: the Mentor Status Checker finds the mentors' course on their WordPress.org profile when it promotes (the daily check does so when Let the daily check also promote mentors is ticked in the tool's settings, and Run check and promote and wp wpcredits check_mentors --promote always do), or an Administrator presses The course is completed on their application, which asks first. It is one step either way, and the mentors sync makes a mentor the same way. It runs in this order, so that a mentor is never kept waiting on Airtable:

  1. The account. The applicant's account is the one that has their email address, else the one named after their WordPress.org username, else the one that holds their profile; where the Mentors row that holds their address is already linked to an account, that account is theirs. With none, an account is made, named after the username, with the Mentor role. An account that exists is linked and given the Mentor role besides its own: no role is taken away, and an Administrator's roles are never touched. A former mentor is a mentor again on their own account. If the account cannot be made, the application stays selected, with the reason on it.
  2. The application moves to Activated, with a line in its history, and the Mentor Status Checker's Slack message names the new mentor.
  3. The invitation. One invitation, which carries the welcome, is queued whatever Invitation emails says, and goes out with the queue, a few at a time. None goes to an Administrator's account, which signs in already, and none goes yet in two cases where the site cannot be sure whose address it would reach: when the account was found by the WordPress.org username alone, which may be somebody else's, and when the Mentors row that holds the applicant's address belongs to one account while another account also answered for the applicant. The mentor is made all the same. The notice after the press, the application's history and its row under Activated say the invitation is held and why, and once an Administrator has confirmed which account is the person's, Send invite or Resend invite on its row in the Mentors screen's Accounts tab sends it. Until then the Invitations card's button, Send invite and Resend invite on ticked accounts and the email queue pass the account over, and the card and the notice after a press say how many they left out.
  4. The Airtable row, last. An account that holds its own Mentors row already, a former mentor's, has that row's Status set back to Active, the status the mentors sync reads, and no search is made; only if Airtable says that row is gone is the table searched, as for anyone else. Otherwise the Mentors table is searched for the applicant's address first. A row that holds it, whatever its Status, is set back to Active and linked to the account; only its Status changes. With none, one new row is written, with the applicant's name, WordPress.org profile, email and Status and their answers whose columns the table has, each shaped as its column takes it. A country, language or contribution area the base does not hold is left out by name, the application says so, and the rest of the row is written. Writing needs the token's data.records:write scope, and reading each column's type its schema.bases:read scope; where the token lacks the second, the row holds the name, profile, email and Status alone. Nothing else in Airtable is ever changed and nothing is deleted; after this the row is Airtable's, and the site never updates it again.

An applicant who is a mentor already, an account with the Mentor role, or an Administrator's, that is active and linked to its Mentors row, is filed under Activated as already a mentor, with a note in the history: nothing is sent, nothing is written to Airtable, and the public figures do not count them as made a mentor. An Administrator who applied keeps their roles and is sent no invitation. Two presses, or a press and the daily check, on one application at the same moment do the step once: the second is told it is in hand. While Make mentors from applications is off nothing is made, and an applicant whose course shows waits under Selected (course pending).

Activated lists the mentors made from applications. The applications still waiting for their Airtable row come first, oldest first; the others follow, the newest mentor first. Fifty are drawn, and a line says how many there are when there are more. Each row shows the account, linked to its profile screen, and the invitation's fate and the Airtable row's. The invitation line counts from the moment the applicant was made a mentor, never from an older invitation to the same address: it says the invitation waits in the email queue; or was sent on a day; or was handed over on a day and the mail log does not say whether it went; or that the site's mail host refused it, so that nothing was sent and the link in any earlier invitation no longer works, with where Send invite or Resend invite is; or that none has gone since, because it was held for a person to confirm the account or was passed over, with where Send invite or Resend invite is. For an Administrator's account it says none is sent, for an account that is gone that none can reach it, and for an applicant filed as already a mentor it says nothing. The Airtable line says whether the row was written, set back to Active or linked, and what was left out of it.

If Airtable refuses the row (a token without write access, a column that refuses a value, a table that cannot be read, the network, or no Airtable connection at all), the mentor is made and invited all the same. The application says Airtable's words, and Write the Airtable row again waits on it under Activated. It searches the table by the address before it writes anything, so a row that a request which died had made is found and never made twice. Meanwhile the mentors sync does not unmake the mentor. If it links the account to an Active row itself, that ends the wait, and the application then reads as linked by the mentors sync or by hand, with nothing more to write. An account that is gone has nothing to write for, and the application says so. The Mentors screen's Sync tab says how many mentors are waiting for their row.

Switching it on

Make mentors from applications ships off, and a person switches it on at the launch, in this order:

  1. Before the release that carries it is deployed, the mentor coordinator edits Invitation: mentor in Tools > Emails. Until the deploy the live editor shows the earlier text, with no welcome, so they add the welcome after the invitation's own lines, copied from the release's shipped text of that email, which shows it with one bracketed line where the private links go. They type the courses' invitation links and the mentor resource folder's link in where that line stands, and save. A saved edit is sent in place of the shipped text, welcome or none, so they check that the edit in place is the one they just saved, not an older one. Contact address in emails is set as well, since the welcome asks mentors to reply and a reply reaches that address. From the deploy on, every invitation the mentor's template sends carries the welcome: an activation's, one sent from the Mentors screen, and one the mentors sync queues while Invitation emails is on.
  2. The person running the launch reads the Airtable base's automations, which the site cannot see, so that none fires on the check row of the next step.
  3. They run wp wpcredits mentor_airtable_row --check --email=<the test mailbox's address>, by hand, once. It writes one synthetic row to the Mentors table, with that address and a Status that neither the mentors sync nor the Mentor Status Checker reads, reads it back, deletes it, and says which columns the base kept and which names it would leave out. It may be run against the live base because it only ever deletes the row it just wrote. It changes nothing on the site, and it ends in an error while a row may be left behind, which then has to be deleted in Airtable by hand, and while a column did not take what the site sends. A create that failed on its way to Airtable is said to have failed, never to have been refused, since it may still have reached the base. wp wpcredits mentor_airtable_row <reference> prints the row an application would write, with why the base's columns could not be read when they could not, and writes nothing; it prints the applicant's answers, so use it on a test application.
  4. They switch Make mentors from applications on, and switch off the Airtable automation that emails the welcome, so that a new mentor is not welcomed twice.

Institutions

The Institutions screen is six tabs, and a press on any of them comes back to it, with what came of it said above the tabs. Waiting for review, the tab WPCredits Program > Institutions opens on, holds the queue; the others are Pipeline, Accounts, Semester reports, Agreements and Sync and storage. While Airtable is not connected, every tab says so above the tabs, with the way to the setting. The menu entry carries a bubble counting the applications, the signed agreements and the requests from institutions waiting.

Waiting for review lists the applications from institutions, the signed agreements and the requests from institutions in one list, oldest first, each with how long it has waited and the country's person of contact, for information. An application or a signed agreement is marked overdue once it has waited longer than the days set under Agreement review on the Institutions tab of Settings, and a request from an institution once it has waited longer than fourteen days; an application the anti-spam checks held is marked held, and one that names the same institution or the same address as another in the queue possible duplicate. The queue is read here and decided on the Administrator Dashboard: every row ends with Open on the Administrator Dashboard, the way to the card there that decides it. An application's row also has Open this application, a mentor request's says who the mentor is wanted for and who asked, any other request's says what it asks, the student it is about and who raised it, and a signed agreement's row is the review block the dashboard draws, its checklist, what the scan noticed and the download link, with Open on the Administrator Dashboard where the dashboard's block has Accept it and Return it with this note. While the Administrator Dashboard's page is missing, the list says so once above the rows, and no row links there.

Open this application shows one application in the list's place, with Back to the queue: what the anti-spam checks noticed, whether the applicant has confirmed the address, every answer with the consent (the sentence the applicant agreed to, when, and the policy's address: the WordPress.org privacy policy since 1.123.24, this site's own page, with the date it last changed, for an application filed before), and what Airtable already holds under the same name or address. Under Where it is decided, an open application that the Administrator Dashboard's Institution applications card lists says it is decided there, with the way there. That card lists the fifty oldest open applications, so one past them is decided here, with the same four decisions, Approve, Send this question, Reject and Reject as spam, and each press comes back to the queue. The record-keeping on a closed application stays here: one rejected or marked as spam has Put back in the queue and Delete for good, since the dashboard folds in only the oldest fifty of those, and an approved one has Delete for good, since the dashboard never lists it. Delete for good keeps only the application's reference and the date.

Pipeline lists every institution record by stage, as the last institutions sync read it, and says when that was. Each row gives the institution's country and city, whether Airtable holds a contact address for it, never the address itself, whether it carries the consent tick, when the record was created and the state of its agreement. Confirmed with no agreement recorded narrows the list to those institutions, and Show every stage brings the rest back. Above the stages, Institutions with no live member counts the institutions nobody can act for on this site, with the way to give one an account on the Accounts tab, and a line lists the countries named by institutions that have no Administrator contact in the Countries table. Under the list, Consent counts the records collected before the form asked for consent, and the ones created without the tick since, which is how a record entered by hand in Airtable looks.

Accounts holds the Invitations card, whose button invites every institution account never invited, except one that also mentors and whose invitation was held when an application made it a mentor (the card says how many it left out, and only that account's own row sends it), and the Institution accounts list, under a warning naming any institution account locked out of roster changes for the rest of the day, a lock that lifts by itself the next day. The list works as the Student accounts list does: every institution account, a page at a time, with no email address printed, though the search finds one. Search institutions finds an account by name, username, email address or the name of the institution it acts for. The All, Invited and Never invited views split the list by whether an account has been sent an invitation, each with its count. The list opens sorted by name, A to Z, so a first press on the Name heading turns it Z to A; Username and Institution sort it A to Z, Member since by the day the membership began, the earliest first, and Status puts Active before Membership ended, either followed by locked today for an account locked for the day; pressing a heading again reverses the order. Every sort works on the whole list, never only on the page in view. Screen Options sets how many rows a page holds, 20 by default, and which columns are shown; the Name column cannot be hidden, because each row's actions sit under it.

Under each name are Edit, which opens the account in wp-admin, View page, which opens the Institution Dashboard as the institution the account acts for, while that page exists, Send invite or Resend invite, which emails that one account at once, and Manage members. To invite several, tick them, choose Send invite or Resend invite under Bulk actions and press Apply; both work as they do on the Students screen, through the same queue, and come back to the list as it was. Here too nobody is sent a second invitation within fifteen minutes of the last one, and Resend invite on ticked accounts says how many it left out.

No account, the fourth view, lists institutions rather than accounts: the Confirmed institutions that have no account yet, the ones ready for one first, then by name. Each is shown by its name over its Airtable record ID, with whether Airtable holds a contact address for it under Contact, and under Account either Ready or why it cannot be given one yet, in the words the institutions sync uses. Search institutions finds an institution here by its name, and Institution sorts the view by it. To create the missing accounts, tick the ready institutions, choose Create account under Bulk actions and press Apply, or press Create account under one institution's name. View page, under every institution's name here as under an account's, opens the Institution Dashboard as that institution, while that page exists. Each account is made from the Contact Email Airtable holds, with an invitation queued for it: a password-set link to that address, which cannot be recalled once sent, as the view says above the list. One press creates at most 25 accounts, and the rest stay listed. While any institution on the view has no agreement recorded, the view names it above the list, with the way to the Agreements tab, and no account is created in bulk until it is recorded. Under the list, the view says whether the institutions sync creates these accounts too, which the Create accounts automatically setting decides, and when the institution records it lists were last read.

Manage members is under every row of the No account view, and under an account's row after its invitation; for an account whose membership ended, it opens the institution the account left, where the account is listed with its Re-add. It shows that institution's members in the list's place, under the institution's name and Back to the accounts, which returns to the list as it stood when Manage members was opened until Remove, Re-add or Add account is pressed on the view, after which it opens the Accounts tab's first page; uploading or withdrawing a signed agreement there keeps the list as it stood. The view shows each member with Remove, which ends their access and keeps their account; the contact Airtable names, when no member holds that address; each former member with Re-add; and Add an account, a name and an email address. Add account creates a new account with a random password and queues its invitation. An address that already has an account is adopted only when that account was a member of this institution before or belongs to a mentor; any other is refused as a conflict, naming the account's username, since an account made by hand is somebody's to explain. An adopted or re-added account that was invited before is not sent another invitation, and the notice says so.

Under the members, a signed agreement that reached the program by email is uploaded on the institution's behalf, and lands in the review queue as the institution's own upload does. Invitations the institution's members have sent their colleagues and that are still pending are not on this view: they are on the Institution Dashboard, where they can be resent or canceled. Unlike the list, the view prints the members' email addresses, because accounts are added and removed by address. For a record the pipeline index does not hold, it says "No institution record has that ID." and points to the institutions sync on the Sync and storage tab.

Semester reports lists every report the site holds, the drafts first, then the sixty most recently edited approved ones: each with its institution, a link that opens the report on the Institution Dashboard as that institution, its semester, whether it is a draft or approved, when it was drafted and whether by the site or an Administrator, when it was last edited, and Ask the students, which writes to the semester's students who wrote feedback and have not said whether it may be used. Under the list, Due for drafting lists the semesters the nightly job would draft, each with Draft now; Draft any semester drafts one the job has not reached; and Report log lists the last twenty things that happened to a report.

Agreements holds three cards. Agreements on file lists every Confirmed institution with no agreement recorded, and its button records them all as signed in one press, with the Drive link to the folder where the signed copies are kept: each institution gets its own recorded agreement, its own line in the audit log and its own Airtable cells, and its account can then be created. Agreement discrepancies lists the institutions whose agreement the site and Airtable's Agreement Status disagree about, each locked until the two agree. Agreement template shows the plugin's copy of the Collaboration Agreement, its version, when it was copied from the Doc and its checksum, and which institutions signed which version.

Sync and storage holds the last sync's error when it ended in one, the Airtable sync card with Sync institutions now, or the run's progress and Cancel sync while one is going, then Reconciliation, the rows where the Students table and Students Reports disagree, as the last students sync found them, with the Students rows that name no institution and a Link for each where linking is safe, and Storage, which says how the signed agreements are kept and whether the host refuses a stranger's request for them, with Run probe to ask the host again.

Sponsors

The Sponsors screen is eight tabs, and a press on any of them comes back to it, with what came of it said above the tabs. Waiting for review, the tab WPCredits Program > Sponsors opens on, holds the queue; the others are Sponsors, Accounts, Offers and codes, Interests, Reports, Agreements and Handbook listing, which is in the bar only while the sponsor tiers are announced, with Sponsor tiers on in Settings. The sponsors' records live on this site: they are listed, added and edited on the Sponsors tab, an approved application creates its sponsor's account and any other sponsor's account is created on the Accounts tab's No account view, and no tab waits for a connection to another service. The menu entry carries a bubble counting the sponsor applications, the signed agreements, the sponsor posts and the sponsor offers waiting and, while Sponsor tiers is on, the events waiting.

Waiting for review holds a card for each kind of item waiting, in the order the Administrator Dashboard draws them, each listing what waits oldest first: Sponsor applications, Sponsor posts to review, Sponsor offers to review, Events, only while Sponsor tiers is on in Settings, and Signed agreements. The queue is read here and decided on the Administrator Dashboard, and every item links to its own place there. Sponsor applications lists the companies that applied through the form on the site, each with how long it has waited, its website and contact, and its state. An application the anti-spam checks held is marked held, one that names the same company or the same address as another in the queue possible duplicate, one from a company the site already holds under the same name or website already on the site, one whose contact address already belongs to an account on this site already an account, and one whose approval stopped halfway approval half done. Each row has Open this application and Open on the Administrator Dashboard, the way to its own item on that page's Sponsor applications card, and under the list the same link opens that card. Under it, Recently decided lists the fifty most recently decided applications, marked as spam, rejected or approved, newest decision first, each with Open this application, where one is put back in the queue or deleted for good, and no link to the Administrator Dashboard, which lists open applications only.

Sponsor posts to review lists the posts sponsors wrote and submitted for review, each with its sponsor, who wrote it, when it was submitted and Preview, the way to read it first. Sponsor offers to review lists the offers sponsors sent for review and the changes they made to what students see of live ones, the codes they added to an approved offer among them, each saying whether it is a new offer or changes, whose offer it is, who sent it and how long ago. Events lists the co-hosted events sponsors planned that wait for the program's approval, each with its sponsor, who planned it, how long ago and when it takes place, on your own clock. Signed agreements lists each document a company uploaded as the review block a reviewer reads: who uploaded it, when and how large it is, what to read it for, what the scan noticed in the file and Download the signed agreement. Every post, offer, event and document ends with Open on the Administrator Dashboard, the way to its own item there, where a post is published or returned, an offer or a change approved or returned, an event approved or returned, and a document accepted with Accept it or returned with Return it with this note. Accept it asks before it acts: it names the company, says that the agreement is recorded as accepted with the day's date and how many people at the company are emailed, and that it can be taken out of force on this screen's Agreements tab. Sponsor applications, Sponsor posts to review, Sponsor offers to review and Signed agreements each list no more than the fifty oldest, the ones the dashboard's card lists, and while more are waiting, a line above the list says how many of them it shows and that the next take their place as these are decided on the Administrator Dashboard; on Sponsor applications it adds that the list stops there so that a burst of applications cannot make the screen too slow to open. Events lists every event that waits, as the Administrator Dashboard's card does. The posts, the offers, the events and the agreements are counted up to 200, and past that their count reads 200+. While the Administrator Dashboard's page is missing, the tab says so once above the cards, and nothing on it links there.

Open this application shows one application in the cards' place, with its state, when it arrived and Back to the queue: what the anti-spam checks made of it, every answer with the consent (read as on the Institutions screen), the logo files, and what the site already holds under the same name or website. Under Where it is decided, an open application that the Administrator Dashboard's Sponsor applications card lists says it is decided there, with Open on the Administrator Dashboard, the way to its own item on that card. That card lists the fifty oldest open applications, so an open application past them keeps its decisions here, every decision its state allows, Approve, Send this question, Reject and Reject as spam, and Put back in the queue for one held or waiting on the applicant, and each press comes back to the queue. The record-keeping on a decided application stays here, since the dashboard lists open applications only: one rejected or marked as spam has Put back in the queue and Delete for good, and an approved one has Delete for good. Delete for good keeps only the application's reference and the date, and takes the logo files with it unless the application was approved, when they are the sponsor's logo. An application in a state no decision writes is told only that applications are decided on the Administrator Dashboard, with the way to that card, and while that page is missing, the opened application says so in the link's place.

Sponsors holds, while the move of the sponsor records onto the site is incomplete, the Moving sponsors onto the site box: how far the move got, the sponsors whose old Administrator matched no Administrator on this site, each to be given one on its Edit form, the sponsors still waiting for the first offer in draft that keeps the move open, and Run again. The move runs by itself, trying again at most once a minute, and the box goes once every sponsor has moved. Then the Sponsors card lists every sponsor on the site in a table, with its status, its tier, its product, its program contact, how many accounts act for it and whether its logo is on the site, and Edit and Manage accounts in each row's last cell. A sponsor's name opens the Sponsor Dashboard as that sponsor, while that page exists, and Manage accounts opens its accounts on the Accounts tab. Edit opens the sponsor's form in the card's place, a view of this tab, under Back to the sponsors: what an Administrator owns of the record, with Save and Cancel, then the sponsor's key and listing handle, which nobody edits. Right after Status, on the Edit form and the Add form alike, the box Test sponsor: not listed publicly makes the sponsor a test sponsor, left out of the Partners page, the logo strip, the handbook listing and the public feed, with its offers, posts and events shown to no student or mentor, while its own accounts see their Sponsor Dashboard as usual; the table marks its row "(test sponsor, not listed publicly)", and Test sponsors (1.123.18), in the part of this guide on sponsors further on, says how to test with one. An address that names no sponsor draws the card under a notice that says so. Under the table, Add a sponsor is the form for a company that never applied on the site; nothing else happens when one is added, and the press opens the new sponsor's Edit form. Once its status is Approved, its account is made with Create account on the Accounts tab's No account view.

Accounts holds the Invitations card, whose button invites every sponsor account never invited, except one that also mentors and whose invitation was held when an application made it a mentor (the card says how many it left out, and only that account's own row sends it), and the Sponsor accounts list, under a warning naming any sponsor account locked out of changes for the rest of the day, a lock that lifts by itself the next day. The card and the list's Send invite and Resend invite are new for sponsor accounts in 1.122.0: before, a sponsor account was sent only the invitation queued when it was created or attached. The list works as the Student accounts list does: every sponsor account, a page at a time, with no email address printed, though the search finds one. Search sponsor accounts finds an account by name, username, email address or the name of the sponsor it acts for. The All, Invited and Never invited views split the list by whether an account has been sent an invitation, each with its count. Sponsor names the sponsor each account acts for, with the sponsor's status after it in parentheses when it is not Approved, since such a sponsor keeps its accounts until they are removed. The list opens sorted by name, A to Z, so a first press on the Name heading turns it Z to A; Username and Sponsor sort it A to Z, Member since by the day the membership began, the earliest first, and Status puts Active before Membership ended, either followed by locked today for an account locked for the day; pressing a heading again reverses the order. Every sort works on the whole list, never only on the page in view. Screen Options sets how many rows a page holds, 20 by default, and which columns are shown; the Name column cannot be hidden, because each row's actions sit under it.

Under each name are Edit, which opens the account in wp-admin, View page, which opens the Sponsor Dashboard as the sponsor the account acts for, while its membership lasts and that page exists, Send invite or Resend invite, which emails that one account at once, and Manage accounts, for an account whose Sponsor names one. To invite several, tick them, choose Send invite or Resend invite under Bulk actions and press Apply; both work as they do on the Students screen, through the same queue, and come back to the list as it was. Here too nobody is sent a second invitation within fifteen minutes of the last one, and Resend invite on ticked accounts says how many it left out.

No account, the fourth view, lists sponsors rather than accounts: every Approved sponsor that no account acts for yet, the ones ready for one first, then by name. Each is shown by its name over its key, the one the site holds it by, with its contact address under Contact, masked, or no email when it has none, and under Account whether it is Ready, ready with "the account that already uses this address will be attached", or why it cannot be given one yet: the sponsor's record holds no contact address, which is added on its Edit form, or the address belongs to an administrator, who already reaches every sponsor. Search sponsor accounts finds a sponsor here by its name, and Sponsor sorts the view by it. To create the missing accounts, tick the ready sponsors, choose Create account under Bulk actions and press Apply, or press Create account under one sponsor's name; a sponsor that is not ready has no box to tick. Each account is made from the sponsor's contact address, or the account that already uses that address is attached, and an invitation is queued for it unless it was invited before, as the view says above the list while a sponsor on it is ready: "Creating an account emails a password-set link to the sponsor's contact address. An invitation cannot be recalled once sent." The sponsor's first offer is created in draft, and the sponsor's log has a line for it. One press creates at most 10 accounts, and the rest stay listed: when more were ticked, the notice says "One press creates at most 10; tick the rest and press again." It names any sponsor it could not give an account, with why. A ticked sponsor that has had its account since the page was drawn is left alone, and when that leaves no ticked sponsor to give one, the notice says "There was nothing to create."; Create account pressed under such a sponsor's name says "That sponsor already has an account." Under the list, the view says "An approved application creates its sponsor's account. For any other Approved sponsor, this view is the way one is made." Under each sponsor's name are also View page, which opens the Sponsor Dashboard as that sponsor, while that page exists, and Manage accounts.

Manage accounts is under every row of the No account view, under an account's row when its Sponsor names a sponsor, and in the last cell of each row of the Sponsors tab's table; an Administrator reaches the same view from the Sponsor Dashboard's People card. It shows that sponsor's accounts in the list's place, a view of this tab, under the sponsor's name and Back to the accounts, which returns to the list as it stood when Manage accounts was opened until something is pressed on the view, after which it opens the Accounts tab's first page, as it does for a view opened from the Sponsors tab or the People card. Every press on the view comes back to it. Each account is listed by name and email address with Remove, which ends its membership and its right to write posts, and keeps the account. For an Approved sponsor, Attach account attaches the existing account that uses the address typed, and queues an invitation for it unless it was invited before; an address no account uses is refused, since a sponsor's first account is made with Create account on the No account view. Any account can be attached but an administrator's, a student's, an institution representative's or one that acts for another sponsor; a mentor's can. Every account attached to a sponsor has equal power on the Sponsor Dashboard. Under it, the posting switch says whether the sponsor's accounts can write posts in wp-admin, for an Administrator to publish, and Turn posting off or Turn posting on switches it; posting is switched here and nowhere else. A sponsor that is not Approved keeps its accounts, listed with Remove, and the view says no account can be attached to it and its posting cannot be switched. Unlike the list, the view prints the accounts' email addresses, because accounts are attached and removed by address. For an address that names no sponsor, it says "That link names no sponsor on this site." and that a sponsor is added on the Sponsors tab, with the way there.

Offers and codes lists every sponsor offer, the oldest hundred at most, with its sponsor, its kind, codes or one shared for everyone, its state, how many codes are available, claimed and void, the count it warns at and its last day, and, for support, who claimed from it: each person's name and address, the date and the code's last four characters, with Void, which lets the person claim again and keeps the code void for the count. A sponsor's primary offer is marked (primary), and sponsors see counts only. Above the table, a sponsor that has an account and no offer has a button that creates its first offer, in draft, for the sponsor to complete and send for review from the Sponsor Dashboard.

Interests lists what sponsors said they would like to support from the Sponsor Dashboard, the last fifty, newest first, each with when it was sent, the sponsor, who sent it and what it said; each was mailed when it was sent, to the sponsor's assigned Administrator, or, for a sponsor with none, to the addresses in the Interest mail setting or to every Administrator.

Reports holds the Reports card: each sponsor's report, drafted, edited and marked final in an editor that opens in the card's place, a view of this tab, with the way back to the tab.

Agreements shows the standing state of every Approved sponsor's agreement, which is optional: a company's Sponsor Dashboard, offers and codes work without one. Each sponsor's block says what this site holds and offers the one thing that can be done next. An agreement accepted or recorded as on file has Take it out of force, with a note that is emailed to everybody at the company exactly as it is written. An agreement out of force is reinstated on the Administrator Dashboard, under Out of force in its Sponsor Collaboration Agreements card, as the block says, with the way to its own item there, or, while that page is missing, the sentence that says so in the link's place; that page lists the fifty oldest agreements out of force, so one past them has Reinstate here, under a sentence that says why. Reinstate asks before it acts, here and on the Administrator Dashboard alike: "Put this agreement back in force? Everybody at the company is emailed." Any other sponsor has Record it as on file, for a signed copy that predates this site: the link to it in the program's Drive folder, and the day it was signed if the copy says so. A document a company uploaded is not here: it waits on the Waiting for review tab, which this tab links.

Handbook listing, the last tab, holds the sponsors' listing for the handbook while the sponsor tiers are announced.

Tools

The Tools submenu lists the parts of the program that are run and configured on their own rather than belonging to one audience - currently Header notices, Emails, Need help?, the Mentor Status Checker, the Student Duplicate Finder and the Track Builder. Each has its own screen behind an Open tool button. Four of them, the Mentor Status Checker, the Student Duplicate Finder, Need help? and Emails, keep their settings in a Settings section on that screen, rather than on the Settings screen.

Settings

WPCredits Program > Settings. Seven tabs along the top of the screen, in WordPress's own tab bar: Connection, Students and mentors, Institutions, Sponsors, Security, Mail and Advanced, and the screen opens on Connection. Each tab but Mail is a form of its own with its own Save settings button: saving one tab leaves every other tab exactly as it was, and the notice after a save names the tab it saved ("Sponsors settings saved."). A page left open from before an update can post a form that names no tab; it saves nothing, and the notice asks you to reload the page and save again.

Each section of a tab opens with one sentence and a link to its part of this guide, on a site that publishes the guide at /program-manager-guide/. Each setting has one sentence of help under it, and the rest of what there is to know in a Details fold under that, closed until you open it.

A setting that holds something Airtable or the site can list is chosen rather than typed: the base, the tables and their name columns, the statuses and the stages, and the Administrators who are told about agreements, reports and sponsors' mail. When a list cannot be read, the setting is typed as it always was, and a sentence under it says why. A value saved that its list does not hold is still offered, after the list and marked (current), so a Save never drops it.

Four tools keep settings of their own, the Mentor Status Checker, the Student Duplicate Finder, Need help? and Emails, and each keeps them on its own screen, in a Settings section with a Save of its own, rather than on this one: at the top of the screen, or for Emails at the top of its Signature and footer tab. The Connection tab's first line names the four, each a link to its Settings section, and the next part of this guide, on the tools, says what each of those settings does.

The Connection tab

Its first line names the four tools that keep their settings on their own screens. Then two sections, Airtable and Tables, the tab's Save settings, and under it a button of its own, Read the lists from Airtable again.

Airtable

Tables

Each table of the base the plugin reads or writes, chosen from the base's tables with its ID beside its name, and each name column from its own table's columns. When a list cannot be read, the table's ID or the column's name is typed, and a sentence under the field says why: no Personal Access Token or no Base ID is set, Airtable refused the token, the token lacks the schema.bases:read scope or access to the base, the base has no such table or column, or the read failed.

Four of these had no control before 1.117.0 and could only be changed in code: the Tutors, Feedback and Countries tables, and the Countries name column.

The bases, statuses and stages are read from Airtable once a day, the tables and columns every fifteen minutes, and all of them again after a Save of the Connection tab. A read that failed is not asked again for five minutes, so an Airtable that does not answer holds up one draw of a tab, not every one, and the fields stay typed meanwhile. Read the lists from Airtable again, under the tab's Save button, reads them at once: for a status or a stage somebody has just added in Airtable, which cannot be chosen until the lists are read again, or once Airtable answers again.

When its table is chosen from the list, which saves the table's ID, each of the Institutions and Countries name columns can also be set to None (the built-in column), which leaves the setting blank: each is then read from the column the plugin names by default, Name for both, and the Institutions table's by the mentors sync from the table's primary column, which it finds by the table's ID. A table saved by its name, as one typed before 1.117.0 could be, keeps its name column typed: the mentors sync would ask for that column itself, and a blank one names no column.

The Students and mentors tab

Five sections: Who is on the program, When someone leaves, Accounts, Landing pages and Mentor applications. The status lists are shared: a current student is anyone a mentor is currently mentoring.

Who is on the program

  • Currently mentoring - a checkbox list of statuses: the Students Reports table's Status options under From Airtable, and the status of every track the site runs under From the Track Builder, each once. Students holding any of the ticked statuses appear under "Currently mentoring" on their mentor's page. The list keeps the status of every track the site runs: its box is ticked and switched off, with a note naming the track, and a save that would take one out all the same saves everything else, leaves Currently mentoring as it was, and a notice names the track. Take the track off the live site in the Track Builder first, then remove its status. A Settings page left open while a track was published keeps the new status when it is saved, and the Track Builder's list flags a live track whose status is missing from Currently mentoring. Left untouched, the list saves as it is stored; changed on a page left open, it brings back a status somebody removed in the meantime, so reload the page first. When Airtable's statuses cannot be read, the list is a box to type in, one status per line, and a sentence under it says why.
  • Past students - statuses that mean mentoring has finished, from the same two lists. Those students appear in a separate, collapsed section on their mentor's page. Its fold: with none ticked, only current students are shown, and a status in both lists counts as current. No track runs on a past status, so the list never takes the status of a track the site runs: its box is switched off, under one note for the group, "A live track's status cannot be a past status.", and a save that would add one all the same saves everything else, leaves Past students as it was, and a notice names the track. Take the track off the live site in the Track Builder first, then add its status. A status the list already holds is never switched off there, so it can always be taken out. The program's four original tracks always run, so their statuses are never past statuses.
  • Mentor status to sync - chosen from the Mentors table's Status options, Active by default; only mentors holding this status get an account.

Neither Currently mentoring nor Mentor status to sync can be left blank: each is what a sync filters the base by, so a blank one goes back to its default and a notice says so.

When someone leaves

What the sync does with the account of a mentor or a student who is no longer on the program. The answer that removes comes first, and it is the default for both.

  • When a mentor is no longer active - Remove the Mentor role and clear their student list, or Leave the role in place. The account itself is never deleted either way.
  • When a student leaves the program - Remove the Student role, so they lose access to Student-level content, or Leave the role in place. The account itself is never deleted either way, and their program details are kept.

Accounts

  • Invitation emails - Email each new mentor and student a password-reset link as their account is created. Off by default, and worth leaving off unless you mean to email everybody: a first sync creates around ninety accounts at once. Its fold: invitations are queued and sent a few at a time rather than all inside the sync, so a mail limit cannot swallow half of them unnoticed, and you can also invite people one at a time from the Mentors and Students screens, or tick several in the Students or Mentors screen's list and invite them together. A mentor made from an application is sent theirs whatever this says, since it carries the welcome, except an Administrator, and a mentor whose account is not yet confirmed as the person's (see Applications to mentor).
  • Automatic sync - Read Airtable on a schedule, on by default: the students, mentors and institutions syncs every three hours, the mentors run half an hour after the students run. Its fold: the student rows carry what people are shown on their cards, and the students run is the expensive one, reading a WordPress.org profile per mentor, cached for twelve hours; the mentors run reads three Airtable tables and no WordPress.org profile. A run already in progress is left to finish rather than restarted. The students and mentors runs can also be run by hand from the Students and Mentors screens.

Landing pages

Where mentors and students go when they log in. Each switch has the page's address under it, or, when the page is missing, a sentence saying that re-activating the plugin recreates it.
